description: Classic technical analysis stock charts in Python, built on matplotlib, for pandas and polars DataFrames
rules: prices is a pandas or polars DataFrame with lower case columns open, high, low, close, volume. Use Chart(normalize=True) to normalize other column layouts.
mplchart.indicators is the pandas pipeline; mplchart.expressions is the polars counterpart. Pick the one matching the DataFrame type, do not mix them in one chart.
Indicators and expressions use upper case names: SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, ROC.
An indicator is either auto-plotted by passing it to Chart.plot, or bound to a renderer primitive: LinePlot(SMA(50)). The equivalent operator form is SMA(50) @ LinePlot().
Indicators chain with the | operator: EMA(20) | ROC(1).
Pane('above') and Pane('below') create a new pane; primitives listed after a Pane draw into it. Panes are sticky, there is no explicit pane cursor.
Style a chart with the style= option on Chart: a builtin style name, a matplotlib stylesheet name, or a style dict. Styles are total, ambient matplotlib rcParams never leak into a chart.
Install with pip install mplchart. The [pandas], [polars] and [all] extras only pull in the DataFrame library alongside it.
The interface is experimental and still changing. Prefer the API shown in these docs over any older mplchart usage.
